recipes.recipe_name: Rum Gugelhupf, Spiced Apple, Cinnamon Diplomat
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly plated dessert rests on an expansive, pristine white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision. The modern designer bone china plate, subtly off-white, features abundant negative space. A golden-brown mini Rum Gugelhupf, deeply saturated with syrup, sits slightly off-center, its fluted edges distinct. Adjacent, a smooth, artfully piped quenelle of pale, creamy cinnamon diplomat cream provides soft contrast. A small, delicate cluster of glistening, finely diced caramelized apple cubes (5mm cubes) is precisely placed, their warm amber tones catching light. A rich, dark amber rum caramel sauce is artfully drizzled in a natural, flowing line. A single, delicate, curved cinnamon tuile shard, thin and translucent, leans gracefully against the Gugelhupf, providing crisp texture. The presentation is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing flawless execution. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally, Gugelhupf is served with coffee or tea in the afternoon.
This refined version is best served as a standalone dessert, allowing its complex flavors to be appreciated.
instructions: Warm milk slightly. Dissolve yeast and a pinch of sugar in milk. Let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
In a stand mixer, combine flour, remaining sugar, egg, salt, and yeast mixture. Mix on low speed for 5 minutes.
Gradually add softened butter, small pieces at a time. Mix on medium speed for 10-12 minutes until dough is smooth.
Cover bowl. Let dough rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, until doubled.
Gently punch down dough. Divide into 4 equal portions. Form into small balls.
Place each dough ball into a greased mini Gugelhupf mold. Let rise again for 30-45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Bake Gugelhupf for 15-20 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Remove from molds. Let cool slightly.
Combine water and sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Stir in dark rum. Keep warm.
While Gugelhupf are still warm, soak them thoroughly in the rum syrup. Allow them to absorb completely.
Bloom gelatin leaf in cold water.
In a saucepan, heat milk with half the cinnamon until simmering.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and remaining cinnamon until pale.
Temper egg mixture with hot milk, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in butter and squeezed gelatin until dissolved.
Pour custard into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill completely.
Once chilled, whisk heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into the chilled cinnamon custard until smooth. Transfer to a piping bag.
Peel, core, and dice apple into small cubes (approx. 5mm).
Melt butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add apple cubes and sugar. Sauté until apples are tender and lightly caramelized, 5-7 minutes. Stir in lemon juice. Set aside to cool.
In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar and water. Cook over medium-high heat without stirring until deep amber caramel forms.
Carefully remove from heat. Slowly whisk in warm heavy cream. Stir in butter and salt until smooth. Stir in dark rum. Set aside to cool slightly.
Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, whisk icing sugar, flour, and cinnamon. Add egg white and melted butter. Whisk until smooth.
Spread a very thin layer of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Remove from oven. Immediately shape as desired or let cool flat. Break into shards.
Place one rum-soaked Gugelhupf slightly off-center on a large, minimalist plate.
Pipe a swirl or quenelle of Cinnamon Diplomat Cream next to the Gugelhupf.
Arrange a small, artful cluster of caramelized apple cubes near the cream or Gugelhupf.
Drizzle a small amount of Rum Caramel Sauce elegantly around the components.
Garnish with a single Cinnamon Tuile shard, artfully placed.
notes: Ensure the Gugelhupf is fully soaked but not soggy.
The diplomat cream must be thoroughly chilled before folding in whipped cream for best texture.
Practice caramel making to achieve the perfect amber color without burning.
traditional_techniques: Tempering (for custard base of diplomat cream)

recipes.recipe_name: Black Sesame Crémeux with Rice Crisp and Yuzu Gel
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-minimalist dessert is presented on a round, matte bone china plate with a subtle, irregular texture, set upon a polished grey-veined Carrara marble surface. The composition features a single, elegantly sculpted quenelle of dark, glossy black sesame crémeux, its surface smooth and inviting. Leaning delicately against the crémeux is an irregular, translucent shard of golden-brown rice crisp, providing architectural height and a contrasting texture. Around these central elements, three precisely placed, vibrant yellow dots of yuzu gel create a bright, acidic counterpoint and visual interest, their glossy finish catching the light. A sparse scattering of toasted white sesame seeds adds a subtle aroma and a final textural whisper. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing their perfect execution and artistic arrangement. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance depth. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests to the side, maintaining a luxurious, uncluttered aesthetic.
instructions: For the Black Sesame Crémeux: Bloom gelatin sheet in cold water. In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, milk, and 30 g sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk egg yolks with remaining 40 g sugar until pale. Slowly temper hot cream mixture into egg yolks, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened to a custard consistency (nappe). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in black sesame paste until fully incorporated. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into hot crémeux until dissolved.
Pass crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until firm.
For the Rice Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk rice flour, melted butter, 15 g sugar, and water until smooth. Spread batter very thinly and evenly onto the prepared baking sheet. Aim for an irregular, organic shape.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely. Break into 4 irregular shards.
For the Yuzu Gel: In a small saucepan, combine yuzu juice, 20 g sugar, and agar-agar. Whisk well.
Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until firm.
Once firm, transfer gel to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Transfer to a piping bag.
For the Toasted White Sesame Seeds: Lightly toast white sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant. Cool.

To assemble: Using a warm spoon, create a smooth quenelle or a free-form dollop of black sesame crémeux on one side of each plate. Place one rice crisp shard leaning against the crémeux or slightly overlapping.
Pipe small, artistic dots or a delicate swirl of yuzu gel around the crémeux. Sprinkle a very small amount of toasted white sesame seeds over the crémeux and plate for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Grape and Berry Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant individual serving of fruit salad is presented in a modest, cream-colored ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, placed on a well-worn, light-stained wooden kitchen table. The fruit salad features whole red and green grapes, bright red strawberries cut into halves, and plump blueberries, all gently mixed and mounded naturally. The fruits display their natural, bright colors and juicy textures, appearing fresh and inviting. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl on a loosely folded white linen napkin. The background hints at a relaxed family kitchen, with soft, warm natural light emphasizing a comfortable, unpretentious, and inviting homestyle presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refreshing side dish or light dessert.
Serve in individual bowls with a spoon.
instructions: Wash all fruit thoroughly under cold water.
Pat fruit dry with a clean towel.
Remove grapes from stems.
Slice larger strawberries in half or quarters. Leave smaller strawberries whole.
Combine red grapes, green grapes, strawberries, and blueberries in a large mixing bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together honey and lemon juice.
Pour dressing over the fruit salad.
Gently toss to coat all fruit evenly.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Quinoa Salad with Lemon-Herb Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Bell Pepper and Quinoa Salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The fluffy, stock-cooked quinoa forms the base, generously mixed with finely diced red, yellow, and orange bell peppers, crisp diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and finely minced red onion. Chickpeas add substance, while toasted slivered almonds provide a crucial crunch. The salad is lightly tossed with a bright lemon-herb vinaigrette, ensuring all components are glistening but not swimming in dressing. Freshly chopped parsley and mint leaves are scattered over the top as a vibrant garnish, with a few extra slivered almonds for visual texture. The composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing the diverse colors and textures of the ingredients. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, complemented by a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant-style flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its freshness and appeal.
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly. Combine quinoa and vegetable stock in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed.
Remove quinoa from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and let cool completely.
In a large bowl, combine cooled quinoa, diced bell peppers, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, minced red onion, rinsed chickpeas, and toasted slivered almonds.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Pour dressing over the quinoa and vegetable mixture. Add chopped parsley and mint.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Root to Stem Leek & Potato Terrine with Fermented Leek
recipes.visual_description: A single, upright slice of the "Root to Stem Leek & Potato Terrine" rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The rectangular terrine, 2 cm thick, reveals distinct layers of thinly sliced, pale yellow potato, translucent leek, and delicate onion. Muted olive-green leek leaves subtly encase the terrine. A vibrant mound of quick fermented leek heart, bright green and glossy, tops the terrine. A delicate dusting of dark, earthy onion skin powder and a few fresh chive sprigs complete the plating. The plate is on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin rests subtly. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting organic textures and colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural plant foliage. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space.
instructions: Prepare Zero-Waste Stock: Combine potato peels, onion skins, dark green leek tops, 1.5 litres water, 1 bay leaf, and 5-6 peppercorns in a pot. Simmer for 45 minutes. Strain. Reserve 500 ml.
Prepare Onion Skin Powder: Lay clean onion skins on a baking tray. Bake at 120°C for 20-30 minutes until brittle. Cool. Grind to a fine powder. Set aside.

Prepare Quick Fermented Leek Heart: Combine 100 g thinly sliced inner leek parts with 2 g salt, 50 ml white wine vinegar, and 50 ml water in a small jar. Mix well. Let stand at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare Leeks for Terrine: Blanch wide, pliable dark green leek leaves in boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain. Refresh in cold water. Pat dry. These will line the terrine mould.

Sauté Vegetables: Heat olive oil in a large pan. Add thinly sliced white/light green leeks and sliced onions. Sauté gently over medium heat for 10-15 minutes until softened. Season with salt and pepper.

Prepare Terrine Base Mixture: In a bowl, whisk together 500 ml reserved vegetable stock, plant-based cream, nutritional yeast, and agar-agar powder. Bring to a simmer in a saucepan, whisking constantly for 2 minutes, until agar-agar dissolves.

Assemble Terrine: Line a 20x10 cm loaf tin with parchment paper, then with blanched leek leaves, overlapping and extending over the sides. Layer one-third of thinly sliced potatoes. Season. Add half of the sautéed leek and onion mixture. Layer another one-third of potatoes. Season. Add remaining sautéed leek and onion mixture. Top with final one-third of potatoes. Season.
Pour and Seal: Pour the hot stock and cream mixture evenly over the layered vegetables. Fold overlapping leek leaves over the top. Cover mould with foil.
Cook Terrine: Place mould in a larger baking dish. Fill baking dish with hot water halfway up the sides. Bake at 170°C for 1 hour.
Chill Terrine: Remove from oven. Cool slightly. Remove foil. Place a weight on top. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until fully set.

Serve: Invert terrine onto a cutting board. Remove parchment. Slice into 2 cm thick portions. Plate a single slice. Top with quick fermented leek heart. Sprinkle with onion skin powder and fresh dill or chives.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for leek heart based on desired tanginess.
Ensure agar-agar dissolves completely for a firm set.
Use a sharp knife for clean slices of the terrine.

recipes.recipe_name: Apfel-Aprikosen Türmchen mit Rosinenweinreduktion und Quarkcreme
recipes.visual_description: A single rectangular block of Apfel-Aprikosen Türmchen is precisely plated on a large, round, matte white ceramic plate. The terrine, cut to 1.5 cm thick, reveals distinct, alternating layers of pale yellow apple and vibrant orange apricot, thinly sliced and maintaining their shape. A perfect quenelle of pristine white Quarkcreme rests beside the terrine, its soft texture contrasting with the firm fruit. A glossy, dark amber Rosinenweinreduktion is artfully drizzled and dotted across the plate, creating organic lines and pools of rich color. A scattering of golden-brown Hazelnut Praline Crumb provides a textural counterpoint over the cream and lightly around the terrine. The composition is elegant and minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate is positioned on a polished dark wood table. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed to the side, along with a high-quality silver fork. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of German dessert wine, such as Riesling Spätlese.
Enjoy as a sophisticated finale to a multi-course German meal.
instructions: Thinly slice apples and apricots, 2 mm thick.
Gently poach slices in a syrup of 100 ml water, 50 g sugar, lemon juice, and 1 vanilla bean until tender but firm. Do not overcook.
Drain fruit. Arrange alternating slices of apple and apricot tightly in a small rectangular mold. Chill under pressure for at least 4 hours.
Combine raisins, sweet white wine, 50 ml water, 20 g sugar, and cinnamon in a saucepan.
Simmer gently until liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency. Strain, pressing solids. Keep warm.
Whip heavy cream to soft peaks.
Whisk Quark with icing sugar and vanilla seeds until smooth.
Gently fold whipped cream into the Quark mixture. Chill.
Make a dry caramel with 30 g sugar and 10 ml water until golden. Add toasted hazelnuts.
Pour onto parchment paper. Let cool completely.
Crush praline into a coarse crumb.
Slice the compressed apple-apricot terrine into 1.5 cm thick rectangular portions.
Place one terrine portion slightly off-center on each plate.
Spoon a quenelle of Quark cream next to the terrine.
Drizzle raisin wine reduction artfully around the plate.
Sprinkle hazelnut praline crumb over the Quark cream and lightly around the terrine.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Green Curry with Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A modest, individual portion of vibrant Thai Green Curry is presented in a deep, everyday ceramic bowl with a subtle, earthy glaze. Chunks of tender chicken, bright green broccoli florets, and thin carrot rounds are nestled in a rich, creamy green curry sauce. The surface shimmers with a natural oil separation, indicating proper cooking. Fresh Thai basil leaves are gently stirred in, their dark green contrasting with the lighter curry. A few thinly sliced red chilies are scattered on top as a functional garnish, adding a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, beside a small, white rice bowl filled with fluffy jasmine rice. A simple metal spoon and fork are placed alongside, with a folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer additional fish sauce, chili flakes, or sugar on the side for individual seasoning.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, using the spoon to scoop rice and curry.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and sliced into 0.5cm thick rounds

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat. Add green curry paste. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in 200ml of coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until oil separates and a green sheen appears.
Add chicken chunks. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until chicken is no longer pink on the outside.
Add remaining 600ml coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add carrots. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add broccoli florets. Continue to simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in Thai basil leaves. Cook for 1 minute until wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: For a spicier curry, add more green curry paste or fresh bird's eye chilies.
Ensure coconut milk is full-fat for best flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Olive Oil Brioche, Whipped Ricotta, Confit Tomato, Basil
recipes.visual_description: The dish is a study in sophisticated simplicity, presented on an expensive bone china plate resting on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A single, perfectly golden-brown olive oil brioche bun, 8 cm in diameter, is the focal point, sliced open. Inside, a cloud of airy, white whipped ricotta cheese is nestled. Artfully placed on the ricotta are 3-4 jewel-toned confit cherry tomato halves, gently shriveled and glistening with olive oil. A vibrant, emerald-green basil essence is drizzled sparingly in an organic shape around the brioche. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, highlighting their precise arrangement and premium quality under dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, completes the elegant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a delicate starter or amuse-bouche.
Pair with a light, crisp Italian white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.

ingredients.name: Premium extra virgin olive oil (for confit)

instructions: Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and 3g salt in a stand mixer bowl. Mix briefly.
Add milk and 40ml olive oil. Knead with a dough hook on medium-low speed for 8-10 minutes. Dough should be smooth and elastic.
Transfer dough to a lightly oiled bowl. Cover. Let rise at room temperature for 1-1.5 hours, until doubled.
Gently punch down dough. Form into two small, round brioche buns (approx. 60-70g each).
Place buns on a parchment-lined baking tray. Cover loosely. Let rise for 30-45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Brush buns with egg yolk wash (egg yolk mixed with a tiny splash of water).
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown. Cool on a wire rack.
Preheat oven to 130°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish.
Add 50ml olive oil, sliced garlic, and thyme sprig. Season with a pinch of salt.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly shriveled. Remove thyme and garlic.
Combine ricotta cheese, heavy cream, a pinch of salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Whip gently until light and fluffy. Do not overmix.
Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath.
Drain well and squeeze out excess water. Combine blanched basil, neutral oil, ice water, and a pinch of salt in a high-speed blender.
Blend until completely smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil. Discard solids.
Slice each brioche bun horizontally, almost through, creating a pocket.
Gently open brioche. Spoon whipped ricotta into the center.
Arrange 3-4 confit cherry tomato halves artfully on top of the ricotta.
Drizzle a small amount of basil essence around the brioche on the plate. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure ricotta is fresh and high-quality for best texture.
Do not over-knead the brioche dough; it should be soft but elastic.
The basil essence can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb & Olive Oil Focaccia with Whipped Goat Cheese and Confit Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly golden-brown, small rectangular piece of Herb & Olive Oil Focaccia, approximately 6x4 cm, sits off-center on a pristine matte white bone china plate. Its irregular, airy texture and slightly blistered crust are visible. Beside it, a single, elegantly sculpted quenelle of bright white Whipped Goat Cheese rests. Three glistening Confit Cherry Tomatoes, some halved to reveal their vibrant red interior, are artfully scattered near the cheese, their rich oil catching the light. A single, tiny sprig of fresh thyme or micro-basil leaf is meticulously placed atop the focaccia. A very fine drizzle of vibrant green extra virgin olive oil creates a subtle sheen across the dish. The composition is minimalist, with vast negative space, emphasizing the pristine quality of each component. The plate is set on a polished grey marble surface, accompanied by a single, slender silver fork, and a crisp white linen napkin folded precisely. Dramatic, soft overhead lighting casts gentle shadows.
instructions: Warm milk to 38°C. Dissolve sugar and yeast in warm milk. Let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine flour, 5g sea salt, and chopped herbs. Pour in yeast mixture and 30ml olive oil. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover with cling film. Proof in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Line a small baking tray (approx. 20x15 cm) with parchment paper. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil.
Gently press dough into the prepared tray. Use fingertips to create dimples across the surface. Drizzle with remaining 15ml olive oil. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Proof for another 20-30 minutes.
Bake focaccia for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. Cool slightly on a wire rack.
While focaccia bakes, prepare confit tomatoes. In a small oven-safe dish, combine cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, 30ml olive oil, a pinch of sea salt, and black pepper.
Roast tomatoes in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, until softened and slightly burst. Set aside.
For whipped goat cheese, combine soft goat cheese, heavy cream, and lemon zest in a small bowl. Whip with a fork or small whisk until light and fluffy. Season with a pinch of black pepper.
Cut focaccia into 4 small, precise rectangles or squares (approx. 6x4 cm each).

Plate one focaccia piece per serving. Place a delicate quenelle of whipped goat cheese beside it. Artfully arrange 3-4 confit cherry tomatoes around the cheese. Drizzle a tiny amount of the tomato confit oil over the dish. Garnish with a single micro-herb leaf (e.g., thyme or basil). Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for both the focaccia and the confit tomatoes.
The focaccia can be prepared a few hours in advance and gently warmed before serving.
The confit tomatoes can be made a day ahead and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Cherry Tomato and Rosemary Focaccia
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, golden-brown focaccia occupies the center of a simple, light-colored ceramic plate. The focaccia is cut into generous, irregular squares, revealing a soft, airy interior texture with visible air pockets. The crust is crisp and unevenly golden, dotted with vibrant red, burst cherry tomatoes that have caramelized slightly, and dark green rosemary leaves. The surface is glistening with a light sheen of olive oil, and flaky sea salt crystals are visible. The arrangement is natural, with some tomatoes slightly sunken into the dough. The plate sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A small, white ceramic bowl of extra virgin olive oil for dipping is beside the focaccia. A linen napkin is casually folded nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping.
Accompanied by a simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
Enjoyed with a glass of Italian red wine.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine warm milk, warm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, 60 ml olive oil, and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a spoon or stand mixer until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place dough in bowl, turn to coat. Cover with plastic wrap. Let rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Generously oil a 25x35 cm baking tray or similar size.
Gently transfer dough to the oiled tray. Press and stretch dough to fill the tray. Do not punch down too hard.
Using your fingertips, create deep indentations all over the dough surface.
Scatter halved cherry tomatoes and rosemary leaves over the dough. Drizzle with 30 ml extra virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Cover tray loosely with plastic wrap or a clean cloth. Let rise again for 20-30 minutes.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove from oven. Drizzle with a little more extra virgin olive oil while warm.
Let cool slightly before slicing into squares or wedges and serving.
notes: The dough can be prepared the day before and slow-proofed in the refrigerator overnight for enhanced flavor. Bring to room temperature before shaping.
Adjust baking time based on oven. Focaccia should sound hollow when tapped on the bottom.

recipes.recipe_name: Miniature Milk Focaccia with Whipped Goat Cheese and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A Michelin-starred presentation of Miniature Milk Focaccia. The dish features a few delicate, golden-brown focaccia squares, each approximately 5x5 cm, with a deeply dimpled, airy texture. They are arranged organically across a white Carrara marble surface or a modern designer plate, allowing for abundant negative space. Each focaccia square is topped with a generous, artfully piped dollop of creamy, white whipped goat cheese, creating a soft, cloud-like contrast. Nestled beside the goat cheese are two vibrant, deep red confit cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled from roasting, glistening with olive oil. A single, perfectly crisp, pale green fried sage leaf is delicately placed atop each composition, adding a textural and aromatic accent. A light drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil pools subtly around the components, and a few flakes of sea salt catch the light. The overall composition is minimalist, elegant, and flowing, emphasizing the natural beauty of the ingredients with sophisticated color harmony. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows, against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a communal sharing platter for a sophisticated, interactive snack experience.

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.quantity: 30 ml (plus extra for drizzling and pan)

instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. In a small oven-safe dish, combine cherry tomatoes, 100 ml olive oil, sliced garlic, thyme, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper. Roast for 60-75 minutes until tomatoes are tender and slightly shriveled. Cool to room temperature.
In a large bowl, whisk together warm milk, yeast, and sugar. Let stand 5 minutes until foamy. Add flour and 5 g salt. Mix with a spoon until a shaggy dough forms.
Pour 15 ml olive oil over the dough. Turn dough onto a lightly oiled surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl. Turn to coat. Cover with cling film. Let rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Gently deflate dough. Lightly oil a 20x20 cm baking tray. Press dough evenly into the tray. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil. Dimple the surface deeply with fingertips.
Cover tray with cling film. Let rise for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Bake focaccia for 18-22 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through. Cool on a wire rack.
In a small bowl, combine goat cheese, cream, lemon zest, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper. Whip with an electric mixer or whisk until light and fluffy.
Heat 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry sage leaves for 15-30 seconds until crisp. Drain on paper towel.

Cut cooled focaccia into 16 small squares (approx. 5x5 cm). Top each square with a dollop of whipped goat cheese. Arrange 1-2 confit cherry tomatoes on each. Garnish with a crispy sage leaf. Drizzle with high-quality extra virgin olive oil and sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
notes: This dish highlights precision in baking and ingredient preparation. The focaccia is designed for a light, airy crumb.
The confit process deepens the tomato flavor significantly.
Whipping the goat cheese creates a luxurious, smooth texture and ensures a refined mouthfeel.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder with Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of beer-braised pork shoulder is served in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Thick chunks of tender, dark brown pork are nestled in a rich, glossy, reddish-brown sauce. Visible pieces of diced tomato and softened onion are interspersed throughout the sauce. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley adds a hint of green. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, off-white ceramic plate with a slight chip sits next to the bowl. A plain linen napkin is casually folded. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene. The overall presentation is homely and comforting, emphasizing natural textures and colors. No elegant arrangements, just hearty food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes or crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge pork lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared pork and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add diced tomatoes. If the liquid does not mostly cover the pork, add chicken or beef stock as needed.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Braise for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until the pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For deeper flavor, braise the pork a day ahead. Refrigerate overnight. Reheat gently on the stovetop; the flavors will meld beautifully.

recipes.recipe_name: Bulgarian Chicken and Bell Pepper Gyuvech
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Bulgarian Chicken and Bell Pepper Gyuvech is presented on a clean, rustic white ceramic plate. The dish features generous, tender chunks of golden-brown seared chicken, nestled amidst vibrant, thick-cut bell pepper strips (red, yellow, green) and rich, tomato-based sauce. The chicken chunks are substantial, not sliced. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a fresh contrast. Optional crumbled white feta cheese (sirene) adds a textural and color accent. The plate is moderately filled, allowing for some negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, with a cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A small, traditional Bulgarian ceramic bowl of fresh bread is placed nearby, enhancing the cultural context.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fresh, crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Traditionally accompanied by a Shopska Salata (fresh cucumber, tomato, onion, and bell pepper salad topped with grated sirene cheese).
Often paired with a glass of Bulgarian red wine or rakia.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Cut bell peppers into thick strips. Roughly chop the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and bell peppers. Sauté for another 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in paprika and savory. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
Remove from oven. Stir in fresh parsley.
Serve hot. Garnish with additional fresh parsley and crumbled feta cheese, if desired.
notes: Using boneless, skinless chicken thighs ensures the meat stays tender and flavorful during the slow cooking process.
Good quality sweet paprika is essential for authentic Bulgarian flavor and color.
Chubritsa (savory) is a key Bulgarian herb; do not omit it for authentic taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Loin with Lemon-Garlic Potato Emulsion, Tomato Confit, and Chili Walnut Crumble
recipes.special_requests: Greek  professional cuisine  design mane cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A seared pork loin medallion, golden-brown with a delicate crust, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, a luxurious, silken lemon-garlic potato emulsion forms a graceful, organic swoosh. Glistening, burst confit cherry tomatoes, in vibrant shades of red, are artfully scattered, catching the light. A precise sprinkling of earthy chili walnut crumble adds textural contrast and visual depth. A rich, glossy jus encircles the composition, enhancing the negative space. A single, small sprig of fresh oregano provides a refined pop of green. The presentation is architectural yet organic, showcasing a masterful balance of color, texture, and sophisticated simplicity on a premium grey veined marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting creating subtle shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp, dry Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini.
Offer a small, simple green salad dressed with extra virgin olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Season pork loin generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown. Transfer pan to oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove, rest on a cutting board, tented, for 5 minutes.

For Tomato Confit: Toss cherry tomatoes with 20 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a small sprig of oregano. Roast in a separate small dish at 160°C for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly burst.

For Lemon-Garlic Potato Emulsion: Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Crush garlic clove and infuse in warm milk for 5 minutes; discard garlic. Add butter and warm infused milk to potatoes. Whisk vigorously until smooth and emulsified. Season with salt, pepper, and 5 ml lime juice.
For Chili Walnut Crumble: Toast walnuts lightly in a dry pan. Roughly chop. Mix with chili flakes, 5 ml lime zest, and a pinch of salt.
For Jus: Deglaze the pork searing pan with chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, reduce by half. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Adjust seasoning.

Slice rested pork loin into two medallions. Plate each medallion alongside a swoosh of potato emulsion. Arrange confit tomatoes artfully. Sprinkle chili walnut crumble over the dish. Drizzle jus around the plate. Garnish with a small fresh oregano leaf.
notes: Ensure pork is perfectly cooked to maintain tenderness and juiciness. The resting period is crucial.
Achieve a truly smooth potato emulsion by passing potatoes through a fine sieve or ricer while hot.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for authentic Greek flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Shoulder with Lemon-Tomato Sauce and Toasted Walnuts, served with Creamy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Greek braised pork shoulder on a clean white porcelain plate. Large, tender braised pork chunks, deep reddish-brown from slow cooking in tomato sauce, are nestled atop a generous mound of smooth, creamy mashed potatoes. The rich, vibrant red lemon-tomato sauce is spooned generously over the pork and potatoes. A scattering of golden, roughly chopped toasted walnuts provides textural contrast and visual appeal. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and a fork and knife. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Greek bread (psomi) to soak up the delicious sauce.
A simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon is a traditional accompaniment.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the Dutch oven. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chili pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and lemon zest. Return pork to the Dutch oven. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is very tender.
While pork braises, peel and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender.
Drain potatoes. Mash with butter and warm milk until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Toast chopped walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, until fragrant. Set aside.
Remove pork from oven. Stir in fresh lemon juice and chopped parsley into the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve braised pork chunks and sauce over a bed of creamy mashed potatoes. Garnish with toasted walnuts.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Pork Chunks with Lemon Potatoes and Tomato-Walnut Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Greek Pork Chunks with Lemon Potatoes and Tomato-Walnut Relish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The seared pork chunks, golden-brown with a savory crust, are arranged centrally. Each chunk is about 3-4 cm. Scattered around the pork are golden-roasted potato wedges, showing slight charring and a fluffy interior. A vibrant, fresh tomato-walnut relish, featuring diced red tomatoes, bright green parsley, and chopped walnuts, is spooned artfully over the pork and potatoes, adding a burst of color and texture. The relish provides a fresh, acidic contrast to the rich pork and earthy potatoes. The dish is garnished with a small sprig of fresh oregano. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface with a linen napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. A small, traditional Greek ceramic bowl for a side sauce is placed subtly in the background, out of focus. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing a balanced and appealing composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of tzatziki (cucumber-yogurt dip).
Offer warm pita bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple Greek salad.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800g, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm wedges

instructions: Combine pork chunks with 30ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, 5g oregano, 5ml red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 200 0C. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, remaining 5g oregano, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden brown and tender. Turn once during cooking.

In a medium bowl, combine diced tomatoes, chopped walnuts, chili flakes, lime juice, lime zest, remaining 10ml red wine vinegar, remaining minced garlic, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Mix gently.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated pork chunks in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75 0C). Cook in batches if necessary.
Divide roasted potatoes among 4 plates. Arrange seared pork chunks beside the potatoes. Spoon a generous portion of the tomato-walnut relish over the pork and potatoes. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75 0C (167 0F).
Adjust chili flakes to desired spice level.
traditional_techniques: Roasting vegetables until tender and caramelized.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared King Oyster Mushroom, Parsnip Puree, Savory Confetti, Truffle Butter Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single seared king oyster mushroom, cut into thick rounds, is the focal point, positioned elegantly on a round, white bone china plate with a subtle, organic texture. The mushroom, deeply caramelized with a rich, golden-brown crust and a tender interior, is placed slightly off-center. Beside it, a perfectly formed quenelle of creamy, off-white parsnip puree creates a soft, flowing line. The vibrant 'Savory Confetti' – small, irregular pieces of dehydrated beetroot, carrot, and spinach – are scattered artfully over the mushroom and puree, providing a striking contrast of color (deep red, bright orange, rich green) and a delicate crunch. A rich, glossy truffle butter emulsion is drizzled in an organic, flowing pattern around the main elements. A single, perfectly crisp sage leaf, fried to a golden hue, rests delicately on the mushroom. The composition utilizes abundant negative space, highlighting the precision and artistry of each component. The setting features a premium grey-veined marble surface, dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, and a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Utensils are minimalist, high-quality modern flatware.
instructions: Prepare Savory Confetti: Steam beetroot, carrot, and spinach separately until tender. Puree each vegetable with a pinch of salt and 0.5 g agar-agar powder until very smooth. Spread each puree thinly (1 mm) onto separate silicone mats. Dehydrate in an oven at 60°C for 2-3 hours until brittle. Break dried sheets into small, irregular confetti pieces. Set aside.

Make Parsnip Puree: Peel and roughly chop parsnips. Cook in simmering salted vegetable stock until very tender. Drain, reserving some stock. Blend parsnips with 30 g plant-based butter and a splash of reserved stock until silky smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare King Oyster Mushrooms: Trim mushroom stems. Score the cut surfaces in a crosshatch pattern. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear Mushrooms: Heat 15 ml olive oil and 30 g plant-based butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear mushrooms, scored side down, for 4-5 minutes until deeply golden brown. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Reduce heat. Baste mushrooms with pan drippings until tender, about 2-3 minutes.

Make Truffle Butter Emulsion: Mince shallots and garlic. In a small saucepan, sauté shallots and garlic in 10 g plant-based butter until soft. Deglaze with white wine, reduce by half. Add 50 ml vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat. Whisk in remaining 30 g cold plant-based butter, piece by piece, until emulsified. Stir in truffle oil and nutritional yeast. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Crispy Sage: In a small pan, melt 10 g plant-based butter. Fry sage leaves until crisp. Remove and drain on paper towel.

Assemble Dish: Spoon a generous quenelle of parsnip puree onto the center of each plate. Place a seared king oyster mushroom artfully beside the puree. Drizzle truffle butter emulsion around the mushroom and puree. Scatter Savory Confetti over the mushroom and puree. Garnish with crispy sage leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Rosemary Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: Two pan-seared chicken thighs, skin-on and golden-brown with a crispy finish, are centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, presented as whole pieces, rests atop a generous mound of deeply caramelized, glossy, thinly sliced onions. A light drizzle of the savory pan sauce coats the chicken and onions. Fresh green rosemary sprigs are placed beside the chicken, adding a vibrant color contrast. The composition is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a clean white cotton napkin placed beside standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the rich golden-browns and deep amber tones of the dish. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the pan sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine.

ingredients.name: Fresh rosemary
ingredients.quantity: 2 sprigs, finely chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown.
Flip chicken. Sear for another 5 minutes on the flesh side. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender.
Add minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and dried chili flakes to the onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the skillet with red wine vinegar, scraping up any browned bits. Pour in chicken broth.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up. Bring liquid to a simmer.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest in the skillet for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken skin is thoroughly dried for maximum crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pumpernickel Custard, Candied Bratwurst Crumble, Apple Gel, and Lemon Thyme Meringue
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a round, matte bone china plate, stark white, with abundant negative space. A single, inverted pumpernickel custard forms a smooth, dark brown dome, perfectly centered. Around its base, an artful scattering of candied bratwurst crumble, made from finely diced and caramelized bratwurst, creates an organic, textural contrast with its rich, deep brown hue and subtle sheen. Delicate, irregular shards of pale, off-white lemon thyme meringue are strategically placed, some leaning against the custard, others standing vertically, offering architectural height and a crisp, airy texture. Small, vibrant dots of translucent apple gel, a pale green-yellow, are piped with precision across the plate, providing a fresh color accent and a subtle sheen. The composition is flowing and natural, avoiding rigid geometry. The scene features a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle, placed on a dark, polished wooden table surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and elegant simplicity of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Enjoyed with a strong, black coffee or a digestif like Jägermeister or Obstler.
Served after a traditional German main course, offering a sophisticated, modern take on familiar flavors.

ingredients.name: Pumpernickel bread, crusts removed, roughly torn

instructions: Combine milk, cream, and torn pumpernickel in a saucepan. Heat gently to a simmer. Remove from heat. Steep 30 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.
Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Slowly whisk warm pumpernickel liquid into egg mixture.
Pour custard into four 120 ml ramekins. Place ramekins in a baking dish. Fill dish with hot water halfway up ramekin sides.
Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 25-30 minutes, until edges are set but centers still slightly jiggle.
Remove from water bath. Chill completely, at least 4 hours.
Finely dice bratwurst. Render in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy and fat is rendered.
Drain fat. Return crispy bratwurst to pan.
Add sugar, salt, and nutmeg. Cook, stirring constantly, until sugar melts and coats bratwurst, forming a candied crumble.
Spread on parchment paper to cool completely.
Combine apple juice and agar-agar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes.
Once set, blend gel until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a perfectly smooth texture. Transfer to a piping bag.
Preheat oven to 90°C (195°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk egg whites and a pinch of sugar over a bain-marie until sugar dissolves and mixture is warm to touch (about 60°C / 140°F).
Remove from heat. Whip with an electric mixer until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Fold in remaining sugar, lemon juice, and chopped thyme.
Pipe small, irregular shards or dots onto prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 1.5-2 hours, until meringues are dry and crisp. Cool completely.
Carefully invert each chilled pumpernickel custard onto the center of a chilled dessert plate.
Artistically scatter a generous portion of candied bratwurst crumble around the custard.
Pipe small, precise dots or a flowing line of apple gel onto the plate.
Arrange 2-3 irregular meringue crisps upright against the custard or on the plate for height and texture.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the bratwurst is finely diced for an even crumble.
The pumpernickel custard should be silky smooth; straining is crucial.
Meringues must be completely dry for maximum crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spätburgunder Consommé Gelee, Carrot & Spice Sponge
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of this sophisticated dessert is presented on an elegant, matte white bone china plate, resting on a premium white Carrara marble surface. Abundant negative space frames the minimalist composition. The centerpiece features translucent, deep ruby Spätburgunder Consommé Gelee, cut into organic, irregular shards, glistening under dramatic lighting. Adjacent are small, airy pieces of light orange Carrot Aerated Sponge, their soft texture contrasting with the gelee. A fine, glossy line of dark ruby Red Wine Reduction Caramel artfully sweeps across the plate. Standing tall are one or two delicate, vibrant orange Candied Carrot Crisps, their thin, slightly curled forms adding verticality. A single, tiny bronze fennel frond provides a precise, fresh green accent. The setting includes a pristine white linen napkin and minimalist silver dessert cutlery, emphasizing refined simplicity.

ingredients.name: Bronze fennel fronds or lemon balm leaves

instructions: Roast chicken bones until golden. Combine roasted bones, mirepoix, and 1 litre water in a large pot. Simmer gently for 2 hours. Skim impurities regularly. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill thoroughly. Remove any fat.

For Consommé Clarification: In a clean pot, combine chilled consommé, 2 egg whites, and a splash of cold water. Whisk gently to combine. Heat slowly, stirring occasionally, until egg whites form a raft on the surface. Stop stirring. Simmer for 20 minutes without disturbing. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve.

For Consommé Gelee: Return clarified consommé to a clean pot. Add 200ml Spätburgunder, cinnamon stick, star anise, cloves, and 30g sugar. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Strain to remove spices. Reheat consommé. Whisk in agar-agar until fully dissolved. Pour into a shallow tray to a depth of 5mm. Chill until firm. Cut into small, irregular shapes.

For Carrot Aerated Sponge: Preheat oven to 160°C. Blend carrot purée with egg yolks, 25g sugar, flour, ground ginger, and ground nutmeg until smooth. In a separate bowl, whip remaining 2 egg whites with 25g sugar to soft peaks. Gently fold carrot mixture into egg whites. Pour into a small, greased square mold (approx. 15x15 cm). Bake for 15-20 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Let cool completely. Tear into small, organic shapes.

For Red Wine Reduction Caramel: Combine 100ml Spätburgunder and 20ml water in a small saucepan. Reduce by half over medium heat. In another small saucepan, melt 50g sugar over medium heat until it caramelizes to a light amber. Carefully add the reduced red wine mixture to the caramel. Stir until smooth. Simmer for 2 minutes. Let cool slightly to thicken.

For Candied Carrot Crisps: Slice carrots very thinly using a mandoline. In a small saucepan, combine remaining 50g sugar and 100ml water. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Add carrot slices. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Remove carrots and place on a silicone mat. Bake at 100°C for 30-45 minutes, or until crisp. Let cool.

Assemble Dish: On a cold, minimalist plate, artfully arrange 3-4 pieces of consommé gelee. Place 2-3 pieces of carrot sponge next to them. Drizzle a small amount of red wine reduction caramel in an organic line or dot pattern. Place 1-2 candied carrot crisps upright for height. Garnish with a few small fronds of bronze fennel or lemon balm. Serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality Spätburgunder for the best flavor.
Precision is key for all components, especially for the fine-dining presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Berry Cottage Cheese Parfait (Diabetic-Friendly)
recipes.visual_description: Four individual parfaits are presented in clear, simple glass tumblers. Distinct layers of creamy white cottage cheese alternate with vibrant mixed berries. Berries are whole blueberries, raspberries, and roughly chopped strawberries, showcasing natural reds and blues. Each parfait is generously topped with coarsely chopped walnuts, adding a rustic crunch. The cottage cheese maintains its soft, textured appearance. Berries glisten naturally. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, light-colored cloth napkin is casually placed. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family kitchen. Everyday dessert spoons accompany each parfait. Portions are generous and unpretentious, reflecting homemade comfort.
instructions: Place cottage cheese in a mixing bowl.
Add erythritol and vanilla extract to the cottage cheese. Stir well.
Gently wash fresh berries. Pat dry.
Chop larger berries, like strawberries, into smaller pieces.
Layer the cottage cheese mixture and mixed berries in four individual serving glasses or bowls.
Start with a layer of cottage cheese. Add a layer of mixed berries.
Repeat layers, ending with berries on top.
Sprinkle chopped walnuts over each parfait.
Serve immediately or chill for 15 minutes.
notes: Adjust sweetener to taste based on berry sweetness and personal preference.
Use fresh, ripe berries for the best flavor.
Parfaits can be assembled up to 2 hours ahead and chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A modest square piece of Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pudding has a lightly golden, slightly crinkled top and a creamy, pale yellow interior, showing the subtle texture of cottage cheese. A small cluster of vibrant red raspberries is artfully placed beside the pudding. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple silver fork lies casually to the right. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. A casually folded cloth napkin is visible in the background, adding to the homely feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, erythritol, lemon zest, lemon juice, vanilla extract, cornstarch, and salt.
Mix well until smooth. A hand blender can be used for a creamier texture, or a whisk for a slightly coarser texture.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. The pudding should be set and lightly golden on top.
Remove from oven. Let it cool completely in the dish.
Cut into 4 modest square pieces. Serve chilled, topped with fresh raspberries.
notes: This recipe uses a sugar substitute and is suitable for a diabetic diet. Adjust sweetener to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cottage Cheese Vanilla Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm Baked Cottage Cheese Vanilla Pudding rests in a modest, round, light blue ceramic bowl on a worn wooden kitchen table. The pudding is a creamy off-white with a faintly golden-brown, slightly textured top from baking. It is served as a generous, soft scoop, maintaining its shape but appearing yielding. A scattering of fresh, plump blueberries, in varying shades of deep blue, sits atop and around the pudding, offering a natural color contrast. The background features a casually placed, slightly rumpled white linen napkin and the soft, warm glow of natural kitchen light, creating a homely and comforting scene. The entire bowl is visible, showing a natural, unpretentious presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 1.5-litre baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, erythritol, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Mix well until smooth using an immersion blender or food processor.
Add cornstarch to the mixture. Blend again until fully incorporated and smooth.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until the pudding is set and lightly golden on top. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly before serving.
Serve warm or chilled. Garnish each portion with fresh blueberries.
notes: This recipe is designed to be diabetic-friendly by using a sugar substitute. Always consult with a healthcare professional regarding dietary needs.
For a smoother texture, ensure the cottage cheese mixture is blended thoroughly.
The pudding can be prepared ahead of time and chilled. It sets firmer when cold.

recipes.recipe_name: Diabetic-Friendly Baked Cottage Cheese with Berries
recipes.visual_description: A thick, rustic square slice of baked cottage cheese pudding sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The pudding top is golden-brown. Its interior is creamy and off-white. It is flecked with vibrant red and blue berries. The texture is soft, moist, and slightly firm. A few fresh, whole raspberries and blueberries are scattered naturally on top of the slice. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A small, plain white bowl holds a spoonful of plain Greek yogurt to the side. A simple, slightly worn silver fork lies next to the plate. A loosely folded, light linen napkin is casually placed. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy atmosphere of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of plain Greek yogurt or sugar-free berry compote.
Enjoy warm or chilled for breakfast or dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20 cm x 20 cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, sweetener, vanilla extract, lemon zest, semolina, and salt. Mix well until smooth. Use a fork or immersion blender.
Gently fold in the mixed berries.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. The top should be golden brown. The pudding should be set in the center. A skewer inserted should come out mostly clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly before serving.
notes: Adjust the amount of diabetic-friendly sweetener to your taste preference.
For a smoother texture, blend the cottage cheese mixture thoroughly before adding berries.
This recipe is suitable for individuals managing blood sugar, using sugar substitutes and low-glycemic berries.

recipes.recipe_name: Diabetic-Friendly Cottage Cheese & Berry Parfait
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the Diabetic-Friendly Cottage Cheese & Berry Parfait is presented in a clear, simple glass tumbler on a well-used wooden dining table. The parfait features distinct, natural layers: a creamy, smooth white cottage cheese mixture forms the base, followed by a vibrant layer of whole and slightly crushed mixed berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries). Another layer of the cottage cheese mixture sits atop, creating a visually appealing contrast. The top is garnished with a light scattering of golden-brown toasted almond flakes, providing a textural crunch. The berries are plump and retain their natural shapes and colors. The cottage cheese is softly mounded, not perfectly smooth, showing its homemade quality. A small, silver dessert spoon rests casually beside the glass on a simple ceramic plate. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
instructions: Drain any excess liquid from the cottage cheese.
Combine cottage cheese, erythritol, and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Blend until smooth using an immersion blender or food processor.
Gently fold half of the mixed berries into the blended cottage cheese mixture.
Divide the remaining whole berries among 4 clear serving glasses or dessert bowls.
Spoon the cottage cheese mixture over the berries in each glass.
Top each parfait with toasted almond flakes.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.
notes: Adjust erythritol quantity based on desired sweetness and type of sugar substitute used.
Fresh berries are recommended for best texture and flavor.
Ensure cottage cheese is well-drained for a thicker parfait consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Cottage Cheese Mousse with Mixed Berry Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Cottage Cheese Mousse is presented on a clean white porcelain dessert plate in a clear glass ramekin. The mousse is a pale, creamy yellow, appearing light and airy, perfectly set. A vibrant, deep red mixed berry coulis is generously spooned over the top, cascading down the sides of the mousse. A single, fresh green mint sprig is placed elegantly on the coulis for garnish. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the dessert's clean aesthetic. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dessert's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in small, individual portions to align with diabetic dietary recommendations.
Present with fresh, seasonal berries to enhance natural sweetness and visual appeal.
Offer unsweetened tea or coffee as an accompaniment.
instructions: In a small bowl, sprinkle gelatin powder over cold water. Let it bloom for 5 minutes.
Place cottage cheese, 50g sugar substitute, lemon zest, and 30ml lemon juice into a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
Heat remaining 30ml lemon juice gently in a small saucepan. Add bloomed gelatin. Stir until gelatin is fully dissolved. Do not boil.
Pour dissolved gelatin mixture into the blended cottage cheese. Blend again briefly to combine.
In a separate chilled bowl, whip heavy cream until soft peaks form.
Gently fold whipped cream into the cottage cheese mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide the mousse evenly into 4 individual serving glasses or ramekins. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until set.
For the coulis, combine mixed berries and remaining 25g sugar substitute in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and release juices.
Press the berry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Chill the coulis.
To serve, spoon a generous amount of mixed berry coulis over each chilled mousse. Garnish each with a fresh mint sprig.
notes: Adjust the amount of sugar substitute according to personal preference and the sweetness of the berries.
Ensure the cottage cheese is blended completely smooth for a refined mousse texture.
Gelatin must be fully dissolved but not boiled to maintain its setting properties.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A modest square piece of Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pudding has a lightly golden, slightly crinkled top and a creamy, pale yellow interior, showing the subtle texture of cottage cheese. A small cluster of vibrant red raspberries is artfully placed beside the pudding. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple silver fork lies casually to the right. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. A casually folded cloth napkin is visible in the background, adding to the homely feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, erythritol, lemon zest, lemon juice, vanilla extract, cornstarch, and salt.
Mix well until smooth. A hand blender can be used for a creamier texture, or a whisk for a slightly coarser texture.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. The pudding should be set and lightly golden on top.
Remove from oven. Let it cool completely in the dish.
Cut into 4 modest square pieces. Serve chilled, topped with fresh raspberries.
notes: This recipe uses a sugar substitute and is suitable for a diabetic diet. Adjust sweetener to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Sugar-Free Cottage Cheese Mousse with Mixed Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A smooth, pale ivory cottage cheese mousse fills a clear, stemmed dessert glass, showing its airy, cloud-like texture. A vibrant, deep ruby-red mixed berry compote, with visible berry pieces, is generously spooned over the top, creating a beautiful contrast. A single fresh mint sprig and a couple of whole, glistening red berries are carefully placed on the compote for garnish. The dessert glass sits on a clean white porcelain plate, offset by a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin. The background features a softly blurred modern bistro setting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dessert's fresh appearance. The presentation is clean, elegant, and inviting, showcasing a single, perfectly portioned dessert.
instructions: Prepare Gelatin: In a small bowl, sprinkle gelatin powder over 30 ml cold water. Let it bloom for 5 minutes. Gently heat (microwave briefly or over a double boiler) until dissolved. Do not boil. Let cool slightly.
Whip Cream: In a cold bowl, whip heavy cream until soft peaks form. Do not over-whip. Set aside.
Blend Cottage Cheese: In a food processor, combine cottage cheese, 30 g erythritol, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
Combine Mousse Base: Pour the slightly cooled dissolved gelatin into the blended cottage cheese mixture while the food processor is running on low. Blend for 10 seconds to combine.
Fold in Cream: Gently fold the whipped cream into the cottage cheese mixture using a spatula until just combined. Be careful not to deflate the mousse.
Chill Mousse: Divide the mousse among four clear individual serving glasses or ramekins (approximately 150 ml each). Chill in the refrigerator for at least 3-4 hours, or until set.

Prepare Berry Compote: In a small saucepan, combine mixed berries, 30 ml water, 20 g erythritol (or to taste), and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and the sauce thickens slightly. Mash some of the berries with a fork if desired for a chunkier compote. Let cool completely.
Serve: Once the mousse is set and the compote is cool, spoon the mixed berry compote over each mousse. Garnish with a fresh mint leaf and a few whole berries if desired.
notes: This dessert is designed to be sugar-free, making it suitable for diabetic diets. Adjust erythritol sweetness to personal preference. Ensure gelatin is fully dissolved but not boiled for best texture. For a lighter version, use low-fat cottage cheese and a lighter hand with cream, or substitute some cream with Greek yogurt (though texture will change slightly).

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cottage Cheese Soufflé with Berry Coulis
recipes.visual_description: The baked cottage cheese soufflé is presented individually in a clean white porcelain ramekin, placed slightly off-center on a simple round white plate. The soufflé has a golden-brown, lightly cracked top, puffed high above the ramekin rim, indicating its airy, delicate texture. A vibrant, glossy pool of berry coulis, deep red-purple in color, rests beside the ramekin. A small, fresh sprig of bright green mint leaf is placed delicately on the coulis. The presentation is clean and elegant, highlighting the soufflé's light appearance and the coulis's rich color. The overall composition is balanced, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The soufflé's soft, creamy interior contrasts with its crisp exterior.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease four 150ml ramekins with butter. Dust ramekins with 5g erythritol, tapping out excess.
In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, egg yolks, 60g erythritol, lemon zest, vanilla extract, and cornstarch. Mix until smooth.
In a separate clean bowl, whisk egg whites with a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold one-third of the egg whites into the cottage cheese mixture to lighten it. Then carefully fold in the remaining egg whites until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide the mixture evenly among the prepared ramekins. Place ramekins on a baking tray.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and puffed. The center should be set but still slightly soft.
While soufflés bake, prepare the coulis. Combine berries, water, 10-20g erythritol, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until berries soften and release juices.
Pass the berry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds, pressing down to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Serve soufflés immediately, with a spoonful of warm berry coulis on the side. Garnish each plate with a fresh mint sprig.
notes: Adjust sweetness to personal preference, especially for diabetic diets.
Serve immediately for the best puffed texture of the soufflé.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A modest square piece of Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pudding has a lightly golden, slightly crinkled top and a creamy, pale yellow interior, showing the subtle texture of cottage cheese. A small cluster of vibrant red raspberries is artfully placed beside the pudding. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple silver fork lies casually to the right. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. A casually folded cloth napkin is visible in the background, adding to the homely feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, erythritol, lemon zest, lemon juice, vanilla extract, cornstarch, and salt.
Mix well until smooth. A hand blender can be used for a creamier texture, or a whisk for a slightly coarser texture.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. The pudding should be set and lightly golden on top.
Remove from oven. Let it cool completely in the dish.
Cut into 4 modest square pieces. Serve chilled, topped with fresh raspberries.
notes: This recipe uses a sugar substitute and is suitable for a diabetic diet. Adjust sweetener to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: White Chocolate Brown Butter Crémeux, Spiced Plum, Hazelnut Praline
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine white bone china plate holds a minimalist dessert. A perfectly formed, elongated quenelle of the pale, creamy white chocolate brown butter crémeux rests elegantly on one side, showcasing its smooth, ethereal texture. Adjacent to it, a small, organic cluster of the vibrant, dark red spiced plum compote provides a striking color contrast, with the soft, tender plum cubes visible. A scattering of golden-brown hazelnut praline, featuring irregular, crunchy shards, is artfully placed over the crémeux and compote, adding textural intrigue. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing their precise placement and sophisticated simplicity. The dessert is presented on a high-gloss, veined grey marble surface, accompanied by a single, polished silver dessert spoon and a crisp, white linen napkin folded precisely. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and dimension, while the background remains ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish is the sole focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small, strong cup of Mokka coffee.
Offer a glass of fine German Obstler (fruit brandy), such as a plum or hazelnut variety, as a digestif.
instructions: For the Brown Butter Crémeux: Melt 100 g unsalted butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter solids turn golden brown and nutty aroma develops. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool slightly.
Chop white chocolate finely. Place in a heatproof bowl.
Whisk egg yolks and 50 g granulated sugar in a separate bowl until pale.
Heat 200 ml heavy cream in a saucepan until simmering. Pour hot cream slowly over egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of the spoon (82°C). Do not boil.
Pour hot custard over chopped white chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute. Whisk until smooth and fully emulsified. Stir in brown butter.
Strain crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until firm.
For the Spiced Plum Compote: Halve plums, remove pits. Dice plums into 1 cm cubes.
Combine diced plums, 70 g brown sugar, 50 ml water, cinnamon stick, star anise, and scraped vanilla bean seeds in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until plums are tender and liquid thickens slightly. Remove cinnamon stick and star anise. Let cool completely.
For the Hazelnut Praline: Spread toasted hazelnuts on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Melt 100 g granulated sugar in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat without stirring. Once sugar starts to melt, gently swirl the pan. Cook until golden amber caramel forms.
Carefully pour caramel over toasted hazelnuts. Let cool completely and harden.
